Hi Naomi / Camila —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. High-level takeaways from our side:
- Primary goal: reduce per-conversation inference cost while meeting sub-100ms 95p latency for our live triage use case.
- Must-haves: on-prem option (for PHI), token-level billing visibility, and KV-cache support for conversational continuity.
- Nice-to-haves: automated quantization recommendations and warm-up autoscaling for morning spikes.

We plan a short head-to-head evaluation with three vendors next week. To make the comparison useful for our engineering committee we need a small set of deterministic tests: throughput at 1k concurrent light requests, 95/99 latency profiles at 256/1024 tokens, hallucination rate on our clinical QA prompts, and memory/CPU footprint during long conversations.

Can you share a concise runbook (checklist + endpoints/data formats) so we can spin up the tests without back-and-forth? Also please include any constraints on model variants we should use for parity.

Alex — thank you for the clear summary and for sharing the harness. Quick recap from our side and next steps so the committee has one thread to reference: 

Pain points you called out:
- Cost volatility at token-level when bursty traffic hits public endpoints.
- Latency tail beyond 100ms at higher concurrency for the clinical triage model.
- Compliance requirement: customer-managed keys and VPC-only control plane for production.

Goals we heard:
1) Demonstrate 95p latency < 100ms for 256-token avg requests and document trade-offs when going to 1k concurrent users.
2) Show end-to-end economics (tokens, infra, cache hit rates) for three candidate model setups.
3) Provide a reproducible parity runbook your infra team can run without dev support.

Included in this reply: parity-checklist.xlsx (runbook with test definitions, expected artifacts to collect, and a sample scoring rubric), headtohead-scorecard.csv (empty template to fill with vendor results), and a recorded 30-min clip of our demo where we walked through batching and cache behavior (demo-recording.mp4).

Proposed timeline:
- Thu 5/27: handoff runbook + credentials for staging endpoints (we will provide ephemeral API keys + sample requests).
- Mon 5/31–Wed 6/2: LumenCare runs parity tests.
- Fri 6/4: 30-min readout with engineering committee.

Alex — adding a few concrete test probes and acceptance criteria to reduce interpretation variance during scoring:

Technical probes (short descriptions):
- Cold-start tail: 100 sequential single-stream requests after a 10-minute idle window; record 95/99 latencies.
- KV cache effectiveness: replay a 10k-user small-session workload (avg 6 turns/session) to measure cache hit rate and per-token cost delta.
- Hallucination spot-check: run a 120-case clinical Q/A set (we'll provide the prompt bank) and flag any non-factual completions >2 tokens.
- Memory leak smoke: continuous 1-hour stream at 250 RPS, sampling memory/GPU usage every minute.

Acceptance thresholds (for vendor parity):
- 95p latency <= 110ms for 256-token baseline (we added a small buffer for infra noise).
- Hallucination rate <= 3% on the clinical prompt bank.
- Cache hit rate >= 45% for the replay workload.

I'll seed the parity checklist with those probes and include clear command-line examples for k6/locust that use your harness format. Naomi/Rishi — can you confirm the staging endpoints will be ready by EOD Thu?

Thanks,
Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
